normalisation.emissions_reference: Each model's combined cement, iron-and-steel and aluminium same-year no-CE emissions

emissions_inventories.GCAM: Reported sector CO2 in Mt CO2/yr

normalisation.emissions_context_reference: Unplotted all-industry context retains each model's own all-industry GHG denominator
normalisation.steel_route_reference: Figure 4 uses each model/pathway/year steel route's own no-CE output, not total steel

notes: OMNIA-ENGAGE aggregates EUE, EUM and EUW; GCAM selects its EU-27 aggregate once, without adding the country rows.
The OMNIA EU regions include Greenland, Faroe Islands, Andorra, Monaco and San Marino in the supplied country mapping; these cannot be removed from regional data.
GCAM source LTT scenarios are paired with OMNIA baseline (NDC+LTT); the scenario names alone do not establish identical policy assumptions.
Historical bars use OMNIA 2019 and GCAM 2021 observations separately; no interpolation or historical alignment is imposed.

The total-output comparison selects reported GCAM cement, steel and aluminium parents. Aluminium route coverage remains unconfirmed and is not assumed equivalent to OMNIA primary plus secondary; explicit steel children are selected only by the separate route comparison.
GCAM aluminium energy includes an Unallocated residual between the reported sector total and its reported carrier parents; the residual is not assigned to an unreported carrier.

GCAM aluminium's alumina-refining coverage is unconfirmed. The energy residual has no confirmed process attribution, and cross-model energy/output quotients are apparent ratios rather than harmonised efficiency measures.

Industrial GHG boundaries differ: OMNIA reports Emissions|GHG|Industry; GCAM combines industry energy-demand Kyoto gases with industrial-process Kyoto gases. GCAM has no comparable cement/steel/aluminium GHG decomposition.
Every response uses the same model, climate pathway, production/energy/emissions scope and comparison-year no-CE reference as its denominator.

Component values are signed percentage-point contributions: 100 times the component CE-minus-no-CE change divided by the no-CE sector total. Net values use the same calculation for the sector total and are percentages.

The total-material dataset retains reported GCAM metal totals. The optional steel-route dataset selects explicit primary and secondary children and uses each route's own reference; GCAM aluminium route coverage remains unconfirmed.
GCAM aluminium energy retains an Unallocated contribution from reported sector total minus reported carrier parents; no process or carrier attribution is assumed.
Incomplete inputs retain the source adapter's explicit missing-activity treatment. Nonfinite or nonpositive no-CE sector totals produce gaps for every contribution and net response.
No historical bars or absolute quantities are plotted. Their raw comparison-year values remain in the source CSVs.
All six production panels share one percentage scale; all six energy panels share another common percentage scale.
Figure 1 plots total production responses, with unplotted route contributions retained as context.
Emissions panels a,b compare the combined cement, iron-and-steel and aluminium response for both models; other industry is excluded from numerator and denominator.
Sector contributions and all-industry responses remain unplotted CSV context with ContextOnly=True and Plotted=False.
OMNIA sector GHG is compared with GCAM reported sector CO2; no GHG equivalence or undocumented GWP conversion is assumed.
GCAM cement sums non-metallic-minerals energy CO2 and cement-process CO2; aluminium selects the specific child, without adding its overlapping non-ferrous parent.
gcam_sector_scope_checks.csv verifies the non-metallic-minerals final-energy parent equals its cement child for all selected source years and scenarios.

Under the configured zero policy, missing NDC+LTT aluminium GHG in all three OMNIA EU regions remains provisional zero and affects the plotted three-sector sum; flags and source rows retain that assumption.
The companion absolute-value figures remain in report_figures_europe_comparison_261014.
Figure 4 adds separate primary and secondary steel columns alongside unchanged cement/aluminium responses; all eight panels share one percentage scale.
Figure 4 steel percentages use route-specific denominators and are not additive; they are excluded from percentage-point contribution checks.
steel_route_checks.csv verifies GCAM reported primary plus secondary steel equals its total in every complete selected scenario/year.

OMNIA NDC+LTT no-CE secondary steel is missing in all three EU regions at the comparison year; the percentage is undefined under both zero and preserve policies. Panel g shows a gap and explicit annotation.
Existing Figures 1-3 individual PDF/SVG/PNG/CSV artifacts are preserved after source-CSV and rendered-PNG equality checks when listed in preserve_individual_figures.
